quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a safe driving practice on the interstate?

options.text: Slower traffic must stay in the right lane.
Change lanes without signaling.
If you miss your exit, go to the next exit.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Stay in the right lane if you are driving slower than other traffic. You cannot back up or make a U-turn on the interstate. If you miss your exit, drive to the next one.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving will suffer. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: A steady green light at an intersection means you:

options.text: Must slow down and prepare to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.
May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.
May not turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: May drive through the intersection if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you may drive through if the road is clear. You may also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. When turning, yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and prepare to stop if cars are approaching you.
Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.
Proceed carefully through the intersection without always stopping.
Stop only for traffic on an intersecting road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A stop sign means you must come to a full stop. Let vehicles and pedestrians in or entering the intersection pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Cars on the right move first.
You have the right-of-way.
Let cross traffic pass before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let cross traffic pass before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, you must let other vehicles and pedestrians cross in front of you. Slow down and stop if needed before continuing.

questions.question: Larger vehicles have:

options.text: Larger blind spots.
Smaller blind spots.
No blind spots.
The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.explanation: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger the blind spots. Large trucks and SUVs have areas near the rear that you cannot see in the side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic
Proceed with caution.
Pedestrian crossing
Come to a full stop.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.question: This road sign indicates:

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum safe speed for leaving a highway. In this example, the safe exit speed is 30 mph.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is a driver who:

options.text: Looks at objects off the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while talking to them during driving.
Only watches the vehicle in front of them.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, looking for items in your vehicle, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Always scan the road, check mirrors, and watch your instruments regularly. These safe habits keep you focused on driving.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Increase your speed so you do not cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If you cannot see ahead, pull off the road safely and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No parking.
Divided highway ahead.
Left turn signal.
Yield.

questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign. It tells drivers what they must do. This sign means you cannot park here.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at an empty intersection at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue driving without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle to your right arrives at the intersection at the same time as you, let them go first. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What is this symbol used for?

options.text: Dangerous intersections.
Slow-moving vehicles.
Yield signs.

questions.explanation: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it moves slowly. You may see this on farm equipment, work vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons. During the day it looks orange. At night it looks red.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you drive. Also adjust your seat, fasten your seatbelt, and secure any items. Do not wait until the car is moving to adjust mirrors.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: As speed increases, the chance of death in a crash increases.
As speed increases, you should increase your following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Higher speeds make crashes more deadly. At speeds above 80 mph, you are unlikely to survive a crash. Faster speeds also mean longer stopping distances, so you need more space between you and the car ahead.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Decrease your following distance.
Drive carefully and do not stare at the construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully and do not stare at the construction.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at unusual things. This causes traffic jams. Keep moving and focus on the road.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
They may follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Let emergency vehicles pass by moving to the side. They may give you instructions over a loudspeaker. Multiple emergency vehicles may follow each other, so wait until it is clear before driving.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When traveling through an intersection.
When passing a bicyclist.
When you see a child about to run into the street.
When parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a child about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others when you think they do not see you. For example, honk if a child starts to run into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the center of a road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic is moving in opposite directions. You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map for directions.
Only if you have an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you have an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You can turn in that direction after a complete stop.
You can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop. You cannot turn in the direction of the arrow. Wait for a green signal.

questions.question: Can you use parking lights instead of headlights when driving at night?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You must use your headlights when driving at night or in low visibility. Parking lights only are not allowed.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean?

options.text: Vehicles in both directions may pass.
Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A broken line means you can pass. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One outside mirror eliminates blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can see blind spots in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: All vehicles have blind spots, even with mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles.

questions.question: If pulled over by police, should you exit your vehicle and walk to the officer's car?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Stay in your vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel when stopped by police.

questions.question: Do drivers have to yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You must stop and yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks. You must also yield to pedestrians in unmarked crosswalks on your side of the road when there are no traffic signals.

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the shoulder with no one in it.
When it approaches you, even with lights off.
On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: Stop when a school bus has flashing red lights on a two-lane road. Traffic from both directions must stop while the lights flash or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: What should you always do at a light rail intersection?

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Look both ways before crossing tracks. Obey all signs and signals. Trains, vehicles, and bicyclists share the road.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks are entering.
Truck exit only.
A steep downgrade is ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the road will go steeply downhill. Check your brakes.

questions.question: When entering traffic from a parked spot at the curb, you should:

options.text: Drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a large gap so you can reach the speed of other traffic.
Wait for two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large gap so you can reach the speed of other traffic.
questions.explanation: When you merge into traffic, wait for a gap large enough to match the speed of other vehicles.

questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" can happen when:

options.text: You stare at the road for long periods of time.
You take frequent rest stops.
You get too much sleep before your trip.
You take short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stare at the road for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead without checking all around you. You may zone out and crash into traffic that slows or stops in front of you.

questions.question: What colors are signs that show the distance to the next highway exit?

options.text: Yellow with black letters
Black with white letters
Red with white letters
Green with white letters

questions.explanation: Signs that give directions are green with white letters or symbols.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and crash severity change as speed increases?

options.text: They decrease.
They stay the same.
They increase.

questions.explanation: As speed increases, stopping distance gets longer and crashes become more severe. Serious injury and death are more likely. Keep more distance between you and other vehicles when driving faster.

questions.question: Never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers. It is illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means a ____ light will appear soon.

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: Your car can hydroplane on wet roads at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.explanation: At speeds up to 35 mph, tires push water away. At speeds above 35 mph, tires cannot move water away fast enough. Your tires may lose contact with the road and slide like water skis.

questions.question: When approaching the top of a hill, you should:

options.text: Speed up slightly.
Be ready to stop if needed.
Keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill or around a curve. A vehicle could be stopped just out of sight. Slow down so you can stop if necessary.

questions.question: Do not pass:

options.text: On a hill or curve.
When school bus lights are flashing.
When approaching an intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Never pass on hills or curves, at intersections, before or on railroad crossings, on bridges, or in no-passing zones. Do not pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance ahead.
Fines double in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block intersection.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns drivers that there is low clearance ahead.

questions.question: When approaching an accident scene, what should you do?

options.text: Keep your attention on your driving.
Keep moving.
Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Only stop at an accident if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived yet. Keep your attention on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not stop to look at accidents, fires, or other disasters.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Sitting in driveways with the car running.
Accelerating quickly.
Slowing down gradually.
Braking abruptly.

questions.explanation: Every quick stop uses time and fuel to speed up again. Drivers who look ahead can slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid sudden braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the immediate left of the cab.
Both directly behind the truck and on the immediate left of the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both directly behind the truck and on the immediate left of the cab.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots. The driver cannot see cars behind them. If you drive too close behind a truck, the driver cannot see you. If you cannot see the driver's face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended for driving with what blood alcohol level?

options.text: 0.15 percent or more.
0.08 percent or more.
Any amount.

questions.explanation: There is zero tolerance for alcohol if you are under 21. Any amount of alcohol in your system will result in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and sound your horn.
A bus stop is ahead.
You are entering a school's parking lot.
A school zone is ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign warns drivers that a school zone is ahead. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and look for nearby police cars.
Yield to pedestrians.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: You may turn right or left on a steady green light unless a sign says not to. When turning, yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let them know you're passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up to get in front of them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: When passing a bicycle, slow down and give them plenty of space. Bicyclists have little protection. Passing too quickly or too close can force them off course.

questions.question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?

options.text: Whoever started moving last.
The driver.
Whoever is slower.
The pedestrian.

questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, with or without a crosswalk.

questions.question: What should you do when another vehicle is passing you?

options.text: Brake hard.
Maintain a constant speed.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: When being passed, yield to the passing vehicle and do not speed up. Let them safely merge back into your lane.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you while driving at night, what should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights blind you, look toward the right edge of the road instead of straight ahead. This keeps your vehicle on the road safely until you pass the other vehicle.

questions.question: When are collisions most likely to happen?

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the other traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one driver goes faster or slower than the other vehicles on the road. Driving much faster than traffic increases your crash risk. Driving much slower than traffic also increases risk because other drivers may hit you from behind or swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: When you see a steady green traffic light, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving unless there are vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a green light, let pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection pass first. You can keep driving, but slow down so you can stop if the light changes before you reach it.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian on the road, but an oncoming vehicle is approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at a steady speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: It is best to deal with one hazard at a time. If you want to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is coming, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: When changing lanes, which action should you NOT do?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Give a turn signal to show your intention.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call the police to check if the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and turn signal. Look for other drivers moving into the same lane. Never use your cell phone while driving.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you never do?

options.text: Move into another lane while inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: What type of drug is alcohol?

options.text: A stimulant.
An antihistamine.
A depressant.

questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows your thinking and makes your reflexes slower and unreliable.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Yield.
Stop.
Warning.

questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards or special conditions ahead. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: There are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked vehicles to your right. How should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
Down the middle between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: When oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked vehicles are on your right, steer down the middle between them.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving ability?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold remedies
All of these

questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your driving, including illegal drugs and over-the-counter or prescription medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is a crime.
